newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish deputy PM Ciller faces corruption debate.
newsitem.headline: Turkish deputy PM Ciller faces corruption debate.

text.p: The Turkish parliament will vote this week on whether to begin an inquiry into Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller on corruption charges that could send her to the Supreme Court, parliament officials said on Monday.

They said MPs would decide on Tuesday if a commission should be set up to look into allegations that Ciller abused her position when she was prime minister to benefit from the facilities of the state-run Turban hotel and tourism company.
Parliamentary sources said Ciller was unlikely to lose the vote because she would get the backing of her own True Path Party and its Islamist Welfare Party coalition partners.
Ciller, who is also foreign minister, recently avoided being sent to the Supreme Court in three cases of alleged corruption with the help of Welfare MPs who voted to drop the charges.
The latest accusations, including claims that Ciller ordered Turban empoyees to do work at her family's farm, date back to her three-year spell as prime minister from 1993.

"There is proof that the prime minister of the time, Tansu Ciller, knowingly abused her position by trying to cover up corruption at the general directorate of Turban in which she herself is involved," the main oppposition Motherland Party said in a request for a parliamentary probe.
